evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 component that starts a background worker, but nothing depends on it and it never runs at startup. How do I make Kora always instantiate it?
expected_behavior: Explains that Kora resolves the graph from the root set outwards, so a component with no dependents is never created
Annotates the @Component class (or the @KoraApp/@Module factory method) with @Root from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Implements io.koraframework.application.graph.Lifecycle so init() starts the worker and release() stops it
States explicitly that implementing Lifecycle does NOT make a component reachable
Does not use field injection, classpath scanning, or external-framework lifecycle annotations such as @PostConstruct
Identifies the missing @Root as the cause: nothing depends on the component, so it is pruned from the graph and init() never runs
Adds @Root (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Root) above/below @Component
Explains that the failure is silent - the build is green and no error is logged
Does not claim the Lifecycle interface, the S3 client wiring, or the constructor is at fault
Does not suggest calling init() manually or moving the work into the constructor

evals.query: Create a Kora 2.0 component that opens a connection pool on startup and closes it cleanly on shutdown.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.application.graph.Lifecycle with exactly `void init() throws Exception` and `void release() throws Exception`
Constructs the resource in the constructor and starts it in init(); stops it in release() with a bounded wait
Notes that release runs on graceful shutdown in reverse order of init, only after every dependent has been released
Mentions that a component implementing AutoCloseable also gets close() on release
Does not return a reactive type, CompletionStage, or use suspend in the lifecycle methods
Does not use external-framework lifecycle callbacks
Replaces the reactive signatures with `void init() throws Exception` and `void release() throws Exception`, the actual Kora 2.0 Lifecycle contract
Removes the Mono/Reactor usage entirely rather than keeping it inside the method body
States that Kora 2.0 container contracts are synchronous and executed on virtual threads, so there is no reactive Lifecycle variant
Updates the import to io.koraframework.application.graph.Lifecycle
Does not wrap the reactive call in block() and present that as the migration
Does not claim the 1.x signature still compiles

evals.query: I provide a third-party DataSource from a Kora 2.0 @Module factory method, but it needs init/release hooks and the class cannot implement Lifecycle. How do I give it a lifecycle?
expected_behavior: Changes the factory method return type to Wrapped<DataSource> and returns new LifecycleWrapper<>(instance, initFn, releaseFn)
Imports io.koraframework.application.graph.LifecycleWrapper and io.koraframework.application.graph.Wrapped
Explains that the container unwraps Wrapped<T>, so consumers keep injecting DataSource
Notes that all three constructor arguments are mandatory and that there is no static wrap(...) factory
In Kotlin, passes the three arguments positionally and does not use named arguments on the Java constructor
Does not rely on external-framework init/destroy method attributes

evals.query: I have two implementations of a Cache interface in my Kora 2.0 container and the build fails with an ambiguous dependency. How do I pick which one each consumer gets?
expected_behavior: Introduces marker tag classes and annotates each implementation with @Tag(SomeTag.class) from io.koraframework.common.annotation.Tag
Repeats the matching @Tag on each injection point
Explains that the tag is a Class, not a string, so refactoring and find-usages keep working
Warns that tagging an implementation removes it from every untagged consumer of that interface
Does not import Tag from io.koraframework.common (the annotations live in io.koraframework.common.annotation)
Does not use external-framework qualifier or primary annotations

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 Kotlin file does not compile: `import io.koraframework.common.Tag` and `import io.koraframework.common.Component` are unresolved. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Corrects both imports to io.koraframework.common.annotation.Tag and io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component
States that all Kora 2.0 DI annotations - Component, Module, KoraApp, KoraSubmodule, Root, Tag, Mapping, Conditional, DefaultComponent, FactoryModule - live in io.koraframework.common.annotation
Notes that io.koraframework.common itself holds non-annotation types such as Configurer, Either, Principal and PromisedProxy
Does not suggest that the artifact is missing or that the BOM version is wrong
Does not invent a io.koraframework.common.Tag type

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I see @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) on the S3Client provider inside AwsS3ClientFactoryModule. Does that mean I have to inject S3Client with a tag? And how would I add a second, differently configured S3 client?
expected_behavior: Explains that inside a module supplied by a @FactoryModule method, @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) resolves to the tag of that factory-module method itself
Concludes that because AwsS3ClientModule#awsS3ClientFactoryModule() carries no tag, the S3Client is untagged and is injected as a plain S3Client
Explains that adding a tag to the @FactoryModule method moves the whole family - config, http client, S3Client - under that tag
Shows a second @FactoryModule method with its own @Tag and config path to obtain a second independently configured client
Mentions that @Tag.Factory outside a factory module is a compile error
Does not claim consumers must write @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) at the injection point

evals.query: I want a Kora 2.0 service that receives every Notifier implementation registered in the container and broadcasts to all of them.
expected_behavior: Injects All<Notifier> from io.koraframework.application.graph.All in the constructor
States that All<T> extends Iterable<T> and is NOT a List - no size(), get(int) or stream()
Iterates the All directly, or materialises it explicitly (List.copyOf does not accept an Iterable)
Explains that a plain All<T> collects only untagged components, while @Tag(Tag.Any.class) All<T> collects every implementation
Does not claim All<T> extends List<T> or assign it to a List field without copying
Does not use classpath scanning or reflective container lookups
Identifies that All<T> extends Iterable<T>, not List<T>, so size() does not exist and List.copyOf cannot take it
Either keeps the field as All<Handler> and iterates it, or drains the Iterable into an ArrayList before List.copyOf
Mentions that All is sealed and cannot be implemented; All.of(...) is the way to build one in a test
Does not suggest casting All to List or to Collection
Does not suggest replacing the parameter type with List<Handler>, which is not a collection claim at all

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 CacheManager only sees the untagged caches. I need it to reach ALL caches, including the ones registered under tags.
expected_behavior: Puts @Tag(Tag.Any.class) on the All<Cache> parameter
Explains that an untagged injection point deliberately matches only untagged components, which is why the tagged caches were missing
Notes that Tag.Any is meaningful at the injection point, not as a registration wildcard on a component
Uses @Tag(Tag.Any.class) All<Cache>, not List<Cache>
Does not use qualifier wildcards or a reflective container lookup

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 Java service an AnalyticsTracker dependency may or may not be present in the container. The graph build fails when it is absent. How do I make it optional?
expected_behavior: Marks the constructor parameter with org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable
Notes that JSpecify @Nullable is a type-use annotation, so its position matters
Writes a real fallback path for the null case rather than only a null check
Mentions the Kotlin equivalent is the nullable type AnalyticsTracker?, with no annotation
Does not suggest jakarta/javax/org.jetbrains @Nullable as the Kora 2.0 convention

Does not suggest required=false autowiring; may mention java.util.Optional<AnalyticsTracker> as a supported Java alternative (the processor wraps a nullable claim) but keeps @Nullable as the convention

evals.query:
My Kora 2.0 Java module fails to compile with `error: type annotation @org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable is not expected here`. The method is:

default Reporter reporter(@Nullable Metrics.Registry registry) { ... }
expected_behavior: Identifies that org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable is a TYPE_USE annotation and the nested type must be written Metrics.@Nullable Registry
Gives the corrected signature

Explains the general rule that the annotation attaches to the type, not the declaration, and shows how it changes meaning for arrays and generics (String @Nullable [] vs @Nullable String[], List<@Nullable String>)
Notes that Kotlin expresses this as Metrics.Registry? and must not carry JSpecify annotations
Does not suggest switching to jakarta.annotation.Nullable or javax.annotation.Nullable to dodge the error
Does not suggest removing the nullability marker

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 ApiClient gets recreated every time its AuthConfig refreshes, which is expensive. I want the client to read the latest config without being rebuilt.
expected_behavior: Injects ValueOf<AuthConfig> from io.koraframework.application.graph.ValueOf instead of AuthConfig directly
Calls config.get() at the point of use and does not cache the result in a field
Explains that depending through ValueOf tells the container not to rebuild this component when the wrapped one refreshes
States that ValueOf has only get(), map() and optional() - there is no refresh() on ValueOf; refreshing is RefreshableGraph.refresh(Node)
Does not claim ValueOf exposes refresh()
Does not use @Lazy, ObjectProvider, or a refresh-scope annotation from another framework

evals.query: I want to wrap my Kora 2.0 PaymentGateway component with a metrics decorator during container startup, before anything else uses it.
expected_behavior: Implements GraphInterceptor<PaymentGateway> from io.koraframework.application.graph as a @Component
Overrides afterInit(T) and beforeRelease(T) - not init/release - and neither declares throws Exception
Returns the decorator from afterInit so that every dependent receives it
Explains that afterInit runs after the component's own Lifecycle.init() and before any dependent is created, and beforeRelease runs before its release()
Notes that interceptors are matched by exact declared type and by tag, so a generic GraphInterceptor<T> matches nothing
Notes that an interceptor needs no @Root
Does not use a bean post-processor or a runtime AOP proxy from another framework
Renames the methods to afterInit and beforeRelease, the Kora 2.0 GraphInterceptor contract
Removes `throws Exception` because neither 2.0 method declares checked exceptions and an override cannot add one
Shows the corrected class
Mentions that a checked exception thrown inside afterInit surfaces as IllegalStateException: Graph interceptor failed with checked exception
Does not keep the 1.x method names or claim they still work
States plainly that Context has been removed from the whole Kora 2.0 framework - not just from the HTTP APIs - so there is no io.koraframework equivalent to import
Removes the Context constructor parameter and the Context.current() usage entirely
Keeps @Root and the synchronous Lifecycle methods
If ambient state is genuinely needed, suggests passing it explicitly or using a plain component/ScopedValue rather than reintroducing a framework Context
Does not rewrite the import to io.koraframework.common.Context or any other invented package
Does not claim Context still exists under a different name

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I want a nightly export job to exist in the graph only when export.enabled is true in config. How?
expected_behavior: Creates a component implementing io.koraframework.application.graph.GraphCondition, tagged with a marker class
Returns ConditionResult.matched(reason) / ConditionResult.failed(reason) with meaningful reason strings
Annotates the job with @Conditional(tag = MarkerClass.class) - the attribute is named tag
Keeps @Root on the job, since nothing depends on it
Explains that on a failed condition the factory is never invoked, so there is no instance and no Lifecycle.init()
Notes that exactly one GraphCondition may carry a given tag, and that this is decided at graph init, not live
Does not write @Conditional(MarkerClass.class) positionally
Does not use an external-framework conditional annotation or a property placeholder

evals.query: In Kora 2.0, when the config file changes and the graph refreshes, which components get recreated? I have an HTTP client component that depends only on a JsonMapper, and a PaymentService that depends on PaymentConfig.
expected_behavior: Explains that RefreshableGraph.refresh(node) re-runs the factory of the start node and then recreates a later node only when one of its direct dependencies (or interceptors) now holds a different instance
States that the HTTP client, whose JsonMapper instance did not change, keeps its instance: init() is not called again and it is not released
States that PaymentService is recreated only if the refreshed PaymentConfig is not equals to the previous one, because an equal new value is discarded and the old instance kept
Mentions that consumers depending through ValueOf<T> are never rebuilt and read the new value via get()
Mentions that an equals() that throws does not fail the refresh: it is logged at WARN and the object is treated as changed
anti_behavior: Claims every node reachable from the refreshed node is always recreated
Claims a refresh recreates components that do not depend on the changed config
Invents a refresh() method on ValueOf or a @RefreshScope-style annotation

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 main() calls KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph) and then wants to run a one-off import with a component from the graph, but the code after run() never executes. Why, and what are the options?
expected_behavior: Explains that run(supplier) is run(supplier, true): it blocks the calling thread until the kora-shutdown hook has released the graph
Names the overload KoraApplication.run(Supplier<ApplicationGraphDraw>, boolean keepAlive) and says keepAlive = false returns right after the graph is initialised
Notes that with keepAlive = false the graph is still released by the kora-shutdown JVM shutdown hook on exit
Recommends a @Root Lifecycle component (or keeping the work inside the graph) as the idiomatic way to run startup work, since run() does not hand the graph back to main
If it quotes the startup log, gives 'Application initialized in <n>ms (JVM running for <s>s)' with the duration in real milliseconds
anti_behavior: Claims run() has only the single-argument signature
Suggests wrapping run() in a new Thread or calling System.exit to get past it
Invents a return value from KoraApplication.run

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0: I declared `@Tag(Tag.Any::class) @Component class DataSourceAudit : GraphInterceptor<DataSource>` so it wraps every DataSource, including the ones tagged @Tag(Reporting::class). Is that right?
expected_behavior: Confirms that an interceptor tagged @Tag(Tag.Any::class) intercepts components of every tag and untagged ones, and that KSP applies the same tag matching as the Java annotation processor
Reminds that matching is still by exact declared type, so it catches only components declared as DataSource, not subclasses registered under their own type
Keeps afterInit(value: DataSource): DataSource and beforeRelease with non-nullable types
anti_behavior: Claims KSP matches interceptor tags by strict equality so Tag.Any interceptors miss tagged components
Suggests declaring one interceptor per tag as a workaround

evals.query: Kora 2.0: RedisCache is @Component @Conditional(tag = RedisEnabled.class). CacheFacade takes `@Nullable RedisCache redis` and falls back to Caffeine when it is null. With redis disabled the app does not start: IllegalStateException: Graph node value was not initialized because condition failed: cache.redis.enabled = false. Isn't @Nullable supposed to give me null?
expected_behavior: Explains that both processors generate a nullable single dependency as g.get(node), and GraphImpl throws 'Graph node value was not initialized because condition failed: <reason>' for a condition-failed node, so @Nullable does not turn a failed condition into null
States it is fixed in 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #960): the dependency is generated as Graph.getNullable(node) and receives null, so the first fix is upgrading to RC2
Gives a workaround for staying on RC1: inject All<RedisCache>, which skips condition-failed members, and take the first element if present; or make the consumer @Conditional on the same tag
Applies the same reasoning to Kotlin RedisCache? parameters
anti_behavior: Blames the condition or tells the user to make RedisEnabled always match
Recommends ValueOf<RedisCache> as the fix — its get() throws the same exception for a condition-failed node

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0: I declared `class AuditInterceptor : GraphInterceptor<PaymentClient>` as a @Component. PaymentClient is an interface implemented by `@Component class HttpPaymentClient : PaymentClient`. afterInit is never called. Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that an interceptor applies only to components whose declared type is exactly its intercepted type, in KSP exactly as in the Java processor — HttpPaymentClient is registered under its own class, so GraphInterceptor<PaymentClient> does not match it
Fixes it by intercepting the declared type (GraphInterceptor<HttpPaymentClient>) or by providing the component from a module method declared to return PaymentClient
Notes that tag matching is a separate filter: an untagged interceptor sees only untagged components, @Tag(Tag.Any::class) sees every tag
anti_behavior: Claims the interceptor matches subtypes or implementations of the intercepted type
